added_models.model: HIV-1-infected SCID-hu Thy/Liv humanized mouse (human fetal thymus/liver implant), oral dosing, thymocyte viral RNA, p24 and CA-SP1 cleavage

engagement.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC2080775). Bevirimat is the first-generation sibling, not a tile member; it opens the strip as proxy and scores nothing.
engagement.note: Bevirimat gave dose-dependent inhibition of CA-SP1 cleavage in implant thymocytes; no member drug has been reported in this model.
engagement.short: CA-SP1 cleavage blocked in mouse thymocytes
engagement.quote: Consistent with its mechanism of action, bevirimat caused a dose-dependent inhibition of capsid-SP1 cleavage in HIV-1-infected human thymocytes obtained from these mice.
engagement.reason: No member ever run in it
engagement.judgement: Separate track opened per the checker's missing list: the only animal efficacy model ever used for HIV-1 maturation inhibitors. Its PD readout (CA-SP1 cleavage in infected thymocytes) is direct. No PubMed record reports GSK3532795, GSK3640254 or GSK2838232 in any humanized mouse, so the track stays untested; the paper's own side-by-side with bevirimat 10-day monotherapy patients (resistance absent in both) is a non-member comparison and is not scored. Pending rule question 6 (proxy-only tracks).

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The exposure statement is for bevirimat (non-member); no member exposure target was ever set from this model.
dose.note: Antiviral activity in mice at plasma bevirimat >2 ug/mL for 6 h, stated as achievable in humans; never tested with a member.
dose.short: Mouse-active exposures called achievable in humans
dose.quote: This activity was observed at plasma concentrations that are achievable in humans after oral dosing, and bevirimat was active up to 3 days after inoculation with both WT HIV-1 and an AZT-resistant HIV-1 clinical isolate.
dose.reason: Exposure target set only for bevirimat
dose.judgement: The model stated an exposure target (>2 ug/mL for 6 h after 100 mg/kg) and compared it with human bevirimat PK, but bevirimat is outside the member list, so the cell stays untested. The members' exposure targets came from the serum-shifted cell panel (draft track hiv-gag-polymorph-cell-panel).

efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read; quote as printed in the PubMed abstract ('log(10)'). Proxy compound only.
efficacy.note: Oral bevirimat cut thymocyte viral RNA >2 log10 and spared T cells; SP1/A1V resistance reproduced in vivo. No member drug tested.
efficacy.short: Bevirimat >2 log10 drop in SCID-hu mice
efficacy.quote: Oral administration of bevirimat to HIV-1-infected SCID-hu Thy/Liv mice reduced viral RNA by >2 log(10) and protected immature and mature T cells from virus-mediated depletion.
efficacy.judgement: Withdraws the draft's claim that no animal efficacy model exists for the class: this one did, was cited as ref 52 of Nowicka-Sans 2016, and was not used (or not published) for any second-generation member. Untested rather than empty because the model existed and was used for the class's first-generation compound. HIV-2/SIV Gag is intrinsically resistant (Zhou 2004 Retrovirology; Yang 2023 PLoS One doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0280568), which rules out macaques but not humanized mice.

added_models.model: Population PK + sigmoid Emax exposure-response model fitted to Phase 2a monotherapy viral-load data, with clinical-trial simulation, used to pick Phase 2b doses

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC5848258); 'C24' and 'log10' are subscripts in the original. Opening entry: the model's prediction (no gain above the plateau) had not yet been tested in a separate trial.
dose.note: Emax model of day-10 C24 vs HIV-1 RNA decline put the response plateau at C24 >=500 ng/mL (>=40 mg); Phase 2b doses chosen above it.
dose.short: Emax model: plateau at C24 >=500 ng/mL
dose.quote: An apparent response plateau was achieved at GSK3532795 C24 ≥500 ng/mL. Consistent with dose response, predicted maximum decline in HIV-1 RNA from baseline is approximately 1.7 log10 copies/mL.
dose.judgement: A distinct system from the draft's serum-shifted EC90 target: the exposure-response model is fitted to patient viral loads, then used prospectively to choose the Phase 2b regimen (205891 chose 60/120/180 mg, all above the plateau). Fitted-to-same-patients models are excluded elsewhere in the atlas when they predict nothing new; this one made a prospective regimen prediction that a later trial tested. Registry NCT01803074 results posted 2019-11-25, after the paper.

dose.magnitude_basis: Week-24 HIV-1 RNA <40 copies/mL across 60-180 mg (76-83%) vs the Phase 2a prediction of no additional response above C24 >=500 ng/mL
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC6198970). Paired by me: the Phase 2b paper reports the flat exposure-response but does not itself cite the Phase 2a Emax plateau as the prediction. The regimen was later abandoned for GI intolerability and NRTI-backbone resistance (rule question 3); dose stays same because the exposure target was reached and the Week-24 primary was met.
dose.note: Phase 2b at 60/120/180 mg (all above the plateau) gave 76-83% <40 copies/mL vs 77% on efavirenz, with no exposure-response, as the plateau model predicted.
dose.quote: Efficacy endpoints demonstrated little correlation to GSK3532795 exposure. It is likely that lower doses would need to be studied to elucidate clear exposure-response relationships.
dose.judgement: Model predicted that doses above the plateau would add nothing; Phase 2b found exactly that (little correlation of efficacy with exposure) and the primary endpoint was met at every dose. Scored same, direction only, because the model gave no response-rate prediction. The model may also have placed the plateau too low to be useful for dose discrimination (the authors say lower doses would be needed to see a relationship), which is a limitation, not a contradiction. Year is the registry results posting (2018-09-19); paper epub 2018-10-23.

dose.magnitude_basis: Week-24 Snapshot HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at the three simulation-selected doses vs the DTG+3TC reference, against the simulation's prediction that all doses >=100 mg exceed 75% of maximal effect
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC12675015). The paper states the doses were selected on the basis of clinical trial simulations via population PK and exposure-response modeling, with >=100 mg predicted to exceed the 75% threshold. Small arms (20-22 each); the 200-mg arm fell below the prespecified efficacy threshold. DOMINO (NCT04493216, results 2023-11-18) used the same simulation-selected doses with two NRTIs and matched dolutegravir (draft efficacy track).
dose.note: Trial simulation from Phase 2a popPK/Emax picked 100/150/200 mg fipravirimat as >=75% of max effect; Week-24 response 95/85/77% vs 86% on DTG+3TC.
dose.short: Simulated doses met Week-24 endpoint, 200 mg short
dose.quote: At Week 24, proportions with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL were 95% (21/22), 85% (17/20), and 77% (17/22) in the GSK’254 100-mg, 150-mg, and 200-mg groups, respectively, vs 86% (18/21) in the DTG plus 3TC group.
dose.reason: Simulated doses reached target; 100/150 mg met
dose.judgement: Second member on the same track (fipravirimat, model side Spinner 2022: Emax EC50 ~170 ng/mL, ~43 mg, Phase 2b doses 100-200 mg chosen conservatively above it). The simulation predicted all three doses on the plateau; 100 and 150 mg met the prespecified Week-24 threshold and 200 mg did not (77%, with protocol-defined virologic failure and more GI events), so source_calls_it is partial and the entry stays same (target reached and enough at two of three doses). Year follows the draft's convention for DOMINO: the registry results posting (2023-12-14) is the earliest public patient result; the stated comparison itself is in the 2025 paper (epub 2025-10-17). Not scored on efficacy to avoid double counting the cell-panel track.

added_models.model: Physiologically based biopharmaceutic model (Simcyp v20) of GSK3640254 absorption built from in-vitro solubility/MDCK permeability in biorelevant media, to reproduce the clinical food effect

dose.magnitude_basis: observed/predicted AUC(0-t) and Cmax ratios (0.94 and 0.73) for the 200 mg tablet fed; all PK parameters within 2-fold, 70% within 1.25-fold
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC9965536). The model was developed, qualified and verified on the same healthy-volunteer fasted/fed data it reproduces (NCT03231943 FTIH, NCT04263142 food effect), so this is a retrodiction; the fasted-state profile was over-predicted with conventional media. No prospective use of the model (e.g. a new formulation or meal) was found. First author (Stamatopoulos) and epub date (2023-02-03) verified on the PubMed record.
dose.note: PBBM qualified on FTIH and food-effect data reproduced the 3-4-fold fed increase in fipravirimat exposure within 2-fold; built after the clinical result.
dose.quote: Thus, by using Simcyp® v20 software, the PBBM model accurately predicted the results of the food effect and predicted data were within a two-fold error with 70% being within 1.25-fold.
dose.judgement: In-silico track under the brief's 'in-silico models used to choose doses' category: the model supports the take-with-food regimen used in Phase 2b (DYNAMIC/DOMINO dosed with a low-fat meal). Scored retro, never same, because the clinical food effect (Spinner/Johnson food-effect study, 3-4-fold) was known before the model was built (decision 10). Opens and is compared in the same year, so no separate untested entry. Registry date is the food-effect study results posting (NCT04263142, 2021-03-03), the patient-side datum the model reproduces.

added_models.model: Cross-species preclinical ADME projection (rat/dog/monkey PK, in-vitro microsome/hepatocyte clearance, metabolite profiling) of human disposition and clearance route

dose.magnitude_basis: qualitative plasma metabolite profile and renal excretion route, preclinical species vs human
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC5989765). Qualitative statement only; no predicted human clearance or dose number is given, and the sponsor relied on it to skip urine collection ('preclinical evaluation indicated negligible renal excretion'). Pending rule question 4 (whether a cross-species ADME projection is a model-system track); drop this track if the rule says no. Species not named for the ADME work (6-month rat and 9-month dog are the chronic tox species).
dose.note: Preclinical ADME for GSK2838232 projected CYP3A4/UGT clearance, negligible renal excretion and species-dependent bioavailability; human metabolite profile matched, boosting required.
dose.short: Preclinical metabolite profile matched human plasma
dose.quote: Metabolite profiles observed preclinically were qualitatively similar to those observed in human plasma.
dose.judgement: Placed under dose because the projection set the regimen: predicted CYP3A4-driven clearance translated into the ritonavir-boosted regimen that reached ~8x PA-IC90 at 200 mg + RTV (Johnson 2018), and predicted negligible renal excretion set the clinical sampling plan. The Phase 1 registry records (NCT02289495, NCT02795754) carry no posted results. Checker listed this as a candidate pending a rule decision; kept apart from mi-nonclinical-tox because it predicts disposition, not harm.

dose.magnitude_basis: human hepatic extraction, elimination route and metabolite coverage vs in-vitro and animal ADME prediction
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, no PMC full text). The abstract also states fraction absorbed 0.26, gut escape 0.898 and hepatic extraction 0.00544 were 'all consistent with low in vitro intrinsic clearance in liver microsomes and hepatocytes'. First author (Wen B, epub 2022-09-24) verified on the PubMed record; registry record for the mass-balance study not identified.
dose.note: Human IV-microtracer ADME of fipravirimat: low hepatic extraction and biliary elimination consistent with in-vitro clearance; no human metabolite needed animal qualification.
dose.short: Human ADME matched in-vitro clearance prediction
dose.quote: No major metabolites in human plasma required further qualification in animal studies.
dose.judgement: Second member on the track; strengthening entry, status unchanged. The human study confirmed the unboosted once-daily regimen's basis (low intrinsic clearance, 21.7 h half-life) and that animal metabolite exposure covered every human metabolite (ICH M3 qualification). Same caveat as the 2018 entry: pending rule question 4.

considered_not_added: Rat 6-month and dog 9-month chronic toxicology plus the FDA clinical hold on GSK2838232 Studies 200912/200207 (Johnson 2018): same system as the draft's mi-nonclinical-tox track; a dated event for that track, not a new model system, and the draft is not edited here.

Patient-level baseline Gag genotype (V362I/V370A) predicting reduced response to GSK3532795 (Dicker 2022): the same patient-derived Gag cell panel the draft tracks; a prediction_level=patient entry belongs on hiv-gag-polymorph-cell-panel (rule question 5).
PI-resistant clinical isolates in PBMC/MT-2 (Ray 2017 JAIDS, PMID 28234686) and HIV-1 subtype/clinical-isolate panels (Nowicka-Sans 2016, Dicker 2022): same cell-panel system.

Semi-quantitative CA/SP1 cleavage-kinetics model of Gag polymorph sensitivity (Lin 2016 PLoS Pathog, doi 10.1371/journal.ppat.1005990): an in-silico re-expression of the same panel's MPI and VLP data; its stated correlation 'with observed in vivo MI efficacies' is qualitative (bevirimat vs BMS-955176) with no member-specific patient number, so it adds no comparison the panel track lacks.
Macaque / SIV or HIV-2 models: never run because HIV-2 and SIV Gag are intrinsically resistant (Zhou 2004 Retrovirology; Yang 2023 PLoS One, GSK2838232); no patient comparison exists.

VH-937 (ACS Med Chem Lett 2024) allometric projection of infrequent human dosing, long-acting parenteral platforms in rats (Sci Rep 2024), C-17 amine analogue rat PK (J Med Chem 2022): non-member or analogue compounds with no patient data.

BMS-955176 discovery papers (Regueiro-Ren 2016 ACS Med Chem Lett; 2018 J Med Chem) and GSK3640254 discovery (Regueiro-Ren 2022 J Med Chem): abstracts cite 'favorable pharmacokinetic profile in preclinical species' but state no human PK or dose projection; full text of PMC4904268 not retrievable from Europe PMC, J Med Chem paywalled. Could not verify a numeric cross-species projection; the ADME track rests on Johnson 2018 and Wen 2022 instead.
Thorough-QT study of GSK3640254 (PMID 37961928) and hERG/dog telemetry: no public animal-side prediction to compare, as the draft already notes.
Clinical DDI studies (metabolic probe cocktail, dolutegravir, TAF/FTC, darunavir/ritonavir, oral contraceptives): no in-silico PBPK DDI prediction stated in any abstract, so no model side.
Human challenge, human genetic (loss-of-function), patient-derived organoid or PDX models: none exist for HIV-1 maturation inhibitors.
